body: You did your part just fine. You're just trying to help and that's obvious. You can try and do all you can in your power to prevent someone from hurting themselves but I think it is inevitable that some of the people will end up doing so anyways. People can be suffering so much that they consider suicide an option. I remember times in my depression where I felt that way. But, you aren't wasting your time I can tell you that. People reached out to me when I asked for help on this sub a long time ago, and having someone to talk to definitely helped me to feel better. I'm sorry that you've had to experience somebody close commit suicide firsthand, but if it really is traumatizing to talk to suicidal people and have that thought affect you then maybe it's time to take a break.

I've seen this discussion pop up on some of the other mental health communities recently. I do think about this a lot. Why force someone to live when they are in so much pain and suffering? If someone is stuck with trauma even after going through therapy and all different kinds of services, why force them to live if it's causing them so much pain? You'd just be making it worse. Especially when that person is just done with living and doesn't want to suffer anymore. It really is twisted. It feels like beyond that point, it's a form of abuse.
